aboard the prompt line is `<b>W</b>/<b>S</b> Välj hållplats · <b>E</b> Kliv av där`, `guagua.hint()`) · `<b>E</b> Låna traktorn` (the farmer's tractor, §10.54) · `<b>SPACE</b> Håll i dig!` · `<b>J</b> håll: Jag kan flyga!` (the `<b>` keycap is Luckiest Guy: uppercase; since feature 52 shown on the lighthouse's gallery, after E's prompt when there is one). Order (`updateHud`): talk (a giver's or the gang's), then `Håll i dig!` while the cabin is turbulent and he stands without holding on (Phase 3 r3, §5.7), then the car, interactable (seats, toilets…) and stand prompts; then `fyren.prompt` adds the J hint up there |

**The result line** (feature 4, §10.8): `#score`, low in the middle (bottom 92 px, under the
prompt at 178 px), a cream card with the dive and its sum in Luckiest Guy over the record line
(terracotta, teal for `NYTT REKORD!`). `hud.showScore(main, sub, record, secs = 4.5)` pops it in
(uppercased, §1.3); `hud.hideScore()` takes it down (the judges' `reset`). The sun cream's result
uses it too (feature 35, §10.26: `SOLKRÄM 7 P` over the record, `FÖR MYCKET! –1 P`, `FÖR LITE!`),
and the stunt jumps (feature 40, §10.27): `hud.liveScore(main, secs = 1.2)` keeps `LUFTTID 0,6 S` up
while his car is in the air, the text changed in place with no pop (up `secs` after the last call),
and the verdict's card is a `showScore`.

**The result list** (feature 71, §10.39): `#results`, low in the middle (bottom 96 px, at least
min(460 px, 86 vw) wide), a navy board (`#1b2f6b`) with an ink edge like the cards, as the
television's ski results: the title in yellow Luckiest Guy, one row a competitor (rank, name, club in
Luckiest Guy, time; tabular figures), the row with `me` in sun yellow, then an italic caption line.
`hud.showResults(title, rows, caption, secs = 6)` (rows `{ rank, name, club, time, me }`) pops it in
as `#score` does; `hud.hideResults()` takes it down. Eslövrundan's is the only one.

**The choice menu** (feature 80, §10.43): `#menu`, on the left under Ole's watch (left 22 px, top
140 px, min(370 px, 86 vw) wide), a cream card with an ink edge and the objective card's three-colour
stripe: the title in Luckiest Guy (uppercased), one row a choice (its label left, its `side` right in
tabular figures), the chosen row in sun yellow with an ink edge, then the note and the keys line with
sun-yellow keycaps. `hud.menu({ title, rows: [{ label, side }], sel, note, keys })` slides it in (the
DOM touched only on a change); `hud.menu(null)` hides it. It is chosen with the keys, never the mouse:
a click releases the pointer lock, which pauses the game. Hytt två!'s is the only one.

**The stamp** (feature 40, §10.27): the banner with cls `stamp`: its main a rubber stamp in red
Luckiest Guy (34–64 px), letter-spaced, in an 8 px red double rule on a cream ground, the banner
tilted −8° (cls `stamp fail`, UNDERKÄND: +6°), and the stamp coming down from 2.6 × in 0.2 s
(`stampDown` on the main; the banner itself does not grow in, and goes in 0.08 s). `--banner-drop`
counts its tilt as `multa`'s.

**The hop counter** (feature 8, §10.13): `#takt`, top right under the meter (top 88 px, right 24 px),
a cream card in Luckiest Guy 26 px, while Stig is in the pool fest's ring: `I TAKT {n} / 8`, `OTAKT!`
(cream on red, 0.9 s, with the coin bump) on a hop off the beat, `I TAKT 8 / 8` on teal (0.9 s) on
the eighth. `hud.setTakt(text, flash = '')` (uppercased; null hides it; `flash` `miss` | `goal`).
While it shows the toast column starts at 142 px (`#takt.show ~ #toasts`; the objective card's 196 px
wins when both show).

**The coffee box** (feature 84, §10.44): `#kaffe`, in the same place (top 88 px, right 24 px; 142 px
under the hop counter when both show), an ink card with a sun-yellow border and text (Nunito 800 16 px)
and a cup icon (`.kaffe-icon`), while Stig has coffee from the pool bar: `SVENSKT KAFFE · SPRINT +20 % ·
0:27` (uppercased, whole seconds rounded up), pulsing (`throb`) for the last 5 s. `hud.setKaffe(text,
low = false)` (null hides it; touches the DOM only on a change). While it shows the toast column starts
at 142 px (196 px under both it and the hop counter, `#kaffe.show ~ #toasts`; the objective card's 196
px wins when both show).

**The FÅNGST card** (feature 107, §10.45): `#fangst`, top left under Ole's watch (left 22 px, top 140 px;
196 px under Ole's watch and the collect card when both show, `#klocka.show ~ #collect.show ~ #fangst`),
214 px wide: a cream note with an ink edge, tilted −1.5°, its head `FÅNGST` (Luckiest Guy 22 px,
uppercased) and the count `n/4` in terracotta over a dashed rule, then one row a kind (Nunito 800 15 px:
the name left, `×n` right in tabular figures; a kind not caught yet `???`, greyed and letter-spaced) and,
once all four are caught, `ALLA FYRA!` in red Luckiest Guy, tilted −3°. `hud.setFangst({ title, rows:
[{ label, n }], all })` slides it in (the DOM touched only on a change); `hud.setFangst(null)` hides it.
It never shows with Hytt två!'s menu (Centro Nórdico is far from the pier).

**The binoculars** (feature 108, §10.48): `#kikare`, over everything in the HUD (z-index 4, as Herr
Storch's viewfinder; toasts, bubbles and the prompt are under it), shown while the lifeguard's binoculars
are up. An SVG over the whole screen (viewBox 1600 × 900, `meet`, so the glasses are sized by the height
and the black reaches every edge at any aspect): two round glasses cut out of `#0d0b10` by a mask
(centres (578, 440) and (1022, 440), r 392), a radial shade towards their edges (to 42 % black), and the
aim ring in the middle (r 46: a cream circle and a SunTrip-yellow arc of 7 that fills clockwise from the
top with the hold, `hud.kikareRing(k)`, k 0..1 or null; touched only on a change of 0.02). In the black:
top left the list (`.kk-list`: its head `SPANING` in yellow Luckiest Guy 20 px, uppercased; eight rows
in Nunito 800 14 px, a box before each, cream and checked with a yellow box when found, greyed when not);
bottom middle the bar (`.kk-bar`: a cream pill with an ink edge, Luckiest Guy 17–24 px, `KIKAREN ·
HITTAT n / 8` or `ALLA ÅTTA!`, then ` · ` and the latest find's name in red while it is new); bottom right
the keys (`.kk-keys`: `MUS`/`WASD` Spana · `E` Sänk kikaren, keycaps as the prompt's). Over the glasses'
lower edge, Stig's line (`.kk-line`: "Stig-Helmer: – …", white Nunito 800 17–24 px with a dark shadow, as
the viewfinder's). `hud.setKikare({ title, rows: [{ label, found }], bar, news, line, who, keys })` shows
it (the DOM touched only on a change); `hud.setKikare(null)` hides it and the ring.

**A shift at the packing shed's belt** (feature 109, §10.49) has no element of its own: the objective card
(`SORTERA TOMATER`, `Tomat n / 40 · Lådor n` with n the tomatoes handled, sorted or dropped, and the bar
`TAPPADE n / 8`, its fill the dropped share, orange `#f07a1e`, red `#ff4a3a` from 6), the prompt line (the
keys), the stamp banner (`stamp`, as the stunt jumps', §10.27) for a whole shift, and the score card
(`#score`): `SKIFTET KLART · n LÅDOR · 100 PTA`, `TOMATRAS · n LÅDOR` or `SKIFTET SLUT · n LÅDOR` (one
`LÅDA`), its sub `NYTT REKORD!` (teal) or `REKORD: n LÅDOR`, up until the fade.

**The volleyball board** (feature 111, §10.50): `#volley`, top in the middle where the objective card would
be (no objective card shows in a match: no mission runs and no other free-roam card can), sliding down as
the card does: a cream board with an ink edge and a red-and-white stripe over its top, the two teams in
terracotta Luckiest Guy 15 px (`STIG & OLE`, `BERRA & ROBBAN`, uppercased) round their points in ink
Luckiest Guy 40 px with a dash between, and under them `FÖRST TILL 5` in Nunito 900 13 px, or a point's
reason (`INNE!`, `UTE!`, `I NÄTET!`, `MISS!`, `FEL SERVE!`) in red. A changed point bumps its number (the
`bump` animation, red). `hud.setVolley({ us, them, a, b, sub, why })` shows it (the DOM touched only on a
change); `hud.setVolley(null)` hides it.

**The tourist couple's viewfinder** (feature 110, §10.51): `#kort`, over everything in the HUD (z-index 4,
as the binoculars): a 3:2 frame in the middle (`--fw` × `--fh` px, set from `kort.frame()`: lying 0.72 of
the screen's height, on end 0.82, `.hog`), rounded 12 px, with a thin cream edge, the camera's black
(rgba(14, 11, 17, 0.94), the frame's spread shadow) round it, four cream corner marks and a 52 px focus
ring in it. Over the frame the keys (Nunito 700 14 px, the keycaps as the binoculars'), or a spoken line in
their place while it is up (`.saying`; Nunito 800, the speaker in cream, "Stig-Helmer: – Säg… omelett."),
never over the picture; under it the reading in Luckiest Guy (3vh, 17–24 px): the couple's and the
subject's, green (#8fe08a) when right, salmon red (#ff8a64) when not. A snap (`.frozen`) shows the grabbed
picture in the frame (`.ko-still`, hiding the ring and the corners) and its stamp: a cream plate with a 5 px
border, tilted −7°, Luckiest Guy 5.5vh, green "BRA KORT!" or red, popping in (`koStamp`). `hud.setKort({ fw,
fh, hog, keys, par: [text, ok], sub: [text, ok], line, who, still, stamp: [text, ok] })` shows it (the DOM
touched only on a change, the still apart from the rest); `hud.setKort(null)` hides it.

**Toasts, bubbles and the objective card** (Phase 3):
- **Toasts** (`hud.toast(text, cls = '', secs)`; radio lines are toasts) stay up `secs`, by default
  by length: `min(7, max(2.4, 1 + 0.06 · characters))` s (the 99-character PANIK toast 6.9 s; it was
  a fixed 2.2 s). At most three at once: a fourth fades the oldest out. A dialogue fades out the
  toasts up when it starts (`hud.clearToasts()`; its own cue toasts come after): the GÄSTER n/4
  toasts stood over the julafton party shot. The column starts at 104 px, or at 196 px while the
  objective card is shown (`#objective.show ~ #toasts`; a stage's radio line overlapped the card by
  7×40 px at 1280×720, 115×40 px at 1024×576). **Under a wide banner** (Phase 3 r2): while a
  banner whose layout box reaches the column (`W/2 + width/2 + 12 > W − 24 − min(430, 0.4 W)`;
  never the `intro` card in the top bar) shows, `hud.showBanner` gives it cls `wide` and sets
  `--banner-drop` on `#hud` (half its height + its tilt's reach, 4 %, 13 % for `multa` and `stamp`, of half its
  width + 12 px), and the column starts at `32 % + --banner-drop` (`40 % + …` with the objective
  card), `transition: top 0.25s`. ¡GUARDIA CIVIL!, UPPDRAG KLART!, KVADDAD!, TURBULENS! and
  SKANDALEN TYSTAD covered the radio toasts' portraits and names (~3 900 px² each at 1280×720).
  There, **with the speedo up**, only the newest two live toasts show (Phase 3 r3, CSS
  `:nth-last-child(n+3 of .toast:not(.out))` → `display: none`; the rest come back when the banner
  goes): at 1280×720 a third toast under UPPDRAG KLART! reached 13–35 px into the speedo for the
  banner's 2.4 s (measured: three 2–3-line radio toasts end at y 598, the speedo's top is 563).
  **Cls `alert`** (Phase 3 r3): `TURBULENS!` while a mission stage runs (§5.7 step 1), in Luckiest
  Guy, red, with a red left edge.
- **Speech bubbles** wrap at 300 px (they were one line up to 750 px), are kept on screen (8 px
  margin), under the coins / meter row (top ≥ 96 px) and under a shown objective card they would
  overlap; a stacked bubble with no room left above waits hidden until the ones below it end.
  **Anchor** (Phase 3 r2): the speaker's real head top, `root.localToWorld(0, model.headTop, 0)`,
  so a plane seat, a car seat (scaled about the hips) and a lean count; the tail tip stops 6 px
  above it (`BUBBLE_GAP`; tail 11 px). A flung or fallen body keeps the steady `y + height`, and a
  plain anchor `{ x, y, z, height }` gives its own head height. The old standing height + 0.6 m put
  a seated passenger's bubble ~1.5 m (113 px) up over the bins and Stig's 40–55 px above his head.
  **Tails point at the speaker** (Phase 3 r3): a bubble stacked above another (or held on screen at
  an edge, `|dx| > 4 px`) gets cls `lead` and a longer, slanted tail (`--tx` its base along the
  bottom edge, at most 18 px from a corner; `--tl` its length; `--ta` its angle) from its bottom
  edge to where a plain tail would end over its speaker's head (8 px below an unstacked bubble's
  bottom edge, `TAIL_H`). Older bubbles are drawn on top (`z-index` 100 − the placing order, kept
  inside `#bubbles` by `isolation: isolate`, so `#banner`'s `z-index: 2` still wins), so the tail
  runs behind the bubble below and comes out under it. The plain tail of a stacked bubble pointed
  at the bubble below: Ole's beside Stig ended 72 px (on foot), 43 px (14A/14B) and 48 px (a sedan)
  above Ole's head; now 9 px, as an unstacked one.
  `game.say` keeps a line up at least `1 + 0.045 · characters` s (halved in test mode, like the
  kinds' `lineSecs`): chatter of 97 characters went after the fixed 2.6 s.
- **The objective card** slides up out of view while the letterbox is on (an in-stage talk:
  haggle, collect, interact lines), where only its bar stuck out under the top bar, and comes back
  with the play. Its **timer** shows the whole seconds left rounded up, `ceil(t)` as `m:ss`, red
  (`urgent`) at ≤ 0:10 (Phase 3 r2): a 6 s stage starts at 0:06 and its last second reads 0:01.
  Flooring showed 0:05 at the start and a whole second of 0:00 with the stage still running.

  marknad · `Templo Ecuménico` kyrka · `Gasolina` bensin · `Guardia Civil` guardia · `Vischan`
  vischan · `Grisfesten` grisfest · `Fataga` fataga · `Golfbanan` golf · `Bungalowen` bungalow ·
  `Bygget` bygge · `Drömplanet` dromplan · `Flygplatsen` airport · `Dynerna` dyner ·
  `Faro de Maspalomas` fyren · `Stranden` playa · `Hamnen` hamn. **`Pepes Bodega` bodega only
  after the `bodega` unlock.** Labels whose landmark is missing are skipped with a console warning.
- The names are data in mixed case; hud.js draws them uppercase (Luckiest Guy, §1.3). The layout
  (`layoutLabels`) avoids other landmark dots and, since Phase 3, the giver's "!" and the objective
  star (13 px boxes; their spots in 8 px steps are part of the layout key): on the gate map, the
  first one a player opens, Ole's "!" covered `SÄKE!ETSKONTROLL`.

### 11.7 Banners and end card

- Mission start: `def.title` / `Uppdrag i av 13` (cls `mission intro`): a one-line title card in
  the top letterbox bar while the intro plays (§9.4 item 2), clear of the framed faces and gone
  before stage 0 starts. `#hud #banner.intro`: top 4.5vh, flex row (main + pill), main
  `clamp(22px, 5vh, 40px)`, no tilt.
- Transition: `LAS PALMAS` / `Soldis och 22 grader varmt.` [F*].
- Grisfest end: `MORGONEN EFTER` / `Julafton på Gran Canaria` (the free-roam clock to 08:00, §10.10).
- **The free-roam clock** (feature 30, §10.10), over the black `#fade` (`hud.fade(on)`, 0.6 s
  opacity, `z-index` 1 under the banner's 2): `NÄSTA MORGON` / `Klockan nio, spansk tid` before a
  mission talked to in the evening or at night, `ZZZ…` during the nap (cls `mission`, held until
  hidden).
- **End card** (`game.playEndCard()`, P1, ~10 s, letterboxed): fade to white; camera to `rioCam`
  looking at `rioBoat` with Stig (outfit `rio`), Majsan, Ole (`rio`), Siv placed on the deck and an
  orchestra of busts; tune `samba`; banner `RIO…?` / *"Svenskarna reser inte till någonting… dom
  reser från någonting."* [F] (6 s); fade back; player at `flamencoPool`; banner
  `NUEVA ESTOCOLMO KLARAT!` / `God jul – och tack för resan!`; free roam continues.
  **Wired in Phase 2** (`main.js playEndCard`, called by the runner after the last mission when a
  cue set `endCard`): `shame.clear()`, out of any car, `inDialog` (input frozen), letterbox, every
  toast dropped (`hud.clearToasts()`, Phase 3 r3), white
  flash; sky `sunset`, tune `samba`, Stig `rio` (not persisted), Ole `rio`; Stig, Majsan, Ole and Siv
  on the aft deck at `rioBoat` offsets (0.76, 1.83), (0.45, 2.46), (0, 3.35), (−0.31, 3.98), each
  turned to `rioCam` (Phase 3 r2: one row across rioCam's view at one depth, the couples side by
  side 0.7 m apart and 1 m between the couples, left to right Siv, Ole, Majsan, Stig; the Phase 2
  offsets split the couples and put Majsan half behind Ole, 2.1 m nearer the lens) with every
  `ANIM_FLAGS` pose off (Phase 3 r3: the julafton duet's `wings`, 6 s on Stig and 4 s on Majsan,
  ran on into the card for a player who read on, Majsan's arm across Ole's chest); camera cut from (rioCam, y 3.2) at (rioBoat, y 2.3, z + 1.5); the `S.endCardMain` /
  `S.endCardSub` banner (cls `mission`, 6 s); after 6.6 s another white flash, camera released, sky
  back, `placeNpcs(true)` + `applyOutfits()`, player at `approachSpot('flamencoPool')`, level tune,
  letterbox off, then the completion banner and the `complete` jingle. The runner then shows the
  last mission's held unlock toast (julafton's `Pepes Bodega har öppnat – på baksidan av
  hotellet.`) under the completion banner (Phase 3 r3: unlocked in the frame the card started, it
  lay over the Rio shot for 3.7 s and was gone before the pool). Scenario `endcard` checks the
  card (it calls `playEndCard()` directly, without the runner's unlock).
- Fallback (cut): only the last banner (used when no `endCard` cue fired).
- Width (Phase 3): `width: max-content; max-width: 94vw` (shrink-to-fit at `left: 50%` had only half
  the screen, so a sub longer than its main wrapped at 50 vw: the end card's quote left
  "någonting." alone). `hud.hideBanner()` only drops `show`, so a banner fades where it stood.
- Placement (Phase 2): the banner sits at 32 % of the height, or 40 % while the objective card
  is shown (`#objective.show ~ #banner`), so the two never overlap; it is drawn above the speech
  bubbles (`z-index` 2 inside `#hud`, which is `isolation: isolate`, so the pause and title cards
  still cover it). The end card's banner adds cls `endcard` (top 20 %), clear of the cast and the
  orchestra busts on the wheelhouse roof. A banner wide enough to reach the toast column (cls
  `wide`, Phase 3 r2) moves the column under it while it shows (§11.4 "Under a wide banner").

## 12. Music and sound (src/audio.js; WP-H; all synthesised)

### 12.1 Tunes (`audio.setTune(name)` switches at the next bar; scheduler reads the tune table per bar)

| tune | used | sketch (original material only) |
|---|---|---|
| `muzak` | flight level (gate + cabin), title on a fresh save | 92 bpm bossa-muzak, Dmaj7–Bm7–Em7–A7, soft sine pad chords, brushed hats, a sine "chime" melody every 8 bars. Routed through the **fear low-pass** |
| `sol` | island default, title on an island save | 116 bpm straight-eighths charter schlager in A minor, Andalusian cadence Am–G–F–E; "accordion" lead (detuned square pair, 5 Hz tremolo, low-passed) playing an original 8-bar phrase; conga voice (sine 220→170 / 330→250); "timple" triangle arpeggios; root–fifth bass |
| `skandal` | island pursuit | 132 bpm 2/4 paso-doble feel, Am–E7–Am–Dm–E7; brass stabs (filtered saw), snare rolls (noise). The two-tone siren plays on top |
| `vals` | grisfest night (cue); Stig's beach dream (feature 57, §10.33) | 3/4 at 150 bpm oom-pah, C–G7–G7–C / F–C–G7–C; bass on 1, chord stabs on 2–3, accordion lead |
| `jul` | julafton (cue) | `sol` re-voiced in A major + sleigh-bell noise ticks |
| `samba` | Ole's boombox (cue), Tonga Tonga, Rio card, unlock | 100 bpm, Dm7–G7–Cmaj7–A7; surdo (sine 60→45 Hz) on 2, tamborim (short high noise ticks), agogô (two square tones) |

**Public-domain traditional cues only** (`audio.trad(name)`, one-shot accordion/square melody over
a ducked music bus): `smaGrodorna` (julafton pool dance; and round after round in the pool fest
after the end, §10.13), `hejTomtegubbar` (julafton toast), `helanGar` (faint, end of the buss17
outro). `trad(name, { vol, duck })` returns the length in s (0 with no context, muted or the music
off); `duck` is the music bus's level under it (default 0.3; the pool fest ducks less for a faint far
round); `audio.tradAt` is the audio-clock time of the cue's beat 0 and `audio.clock()` the audio
clock (null while the context is not running); `tradInfo(name)` gives `{ bpm, beats }` (feature 8). **Never** "Freight Train", "Feliz", Kostervalsen or any
Bengt Palmers theme.

Scheduler fixes (Phase 0): catch-up guard `if (next < ctx.currentTime) next = ctx.currentTime +
0.05`; a `TUNES` table + `registerTune(name, def)` so WP-H can add tunes; music bus → `BiquadFilter`
(low-pass, default 20 kHz) → master, for the fear effect.

### 12.2 Per level / per state

- Flight: `muzak`; FLYGRÄDSLA ≥ 70 → `audio.setMusicLowpass(lerp(4000, 600, (v − 70)/30))` and
  `audio.heartbeat()` every 0.8 s (main.updateAudio, Phase 0); below 70 → `setMusicLowpass(null)`.
- **Cabin drone channel** `audio.drone(level 0..1, bright 0..1)`: a looped 2 s noise buffer through
  a low-pass 300 → 900 Hz (bright) + a 45 Hz saw at low gain; gain `level·0.08`. **Not** touched by
  `main.updateAudio()` (which zeroes the car engine every frame on foot). Silenced by `pause()` and
  by `setLevel('island')`. Cabin levels: gate 0.25 (APU-less DC-8: an external ground unit hum),
  takeoff 0.9/1.0, climb 0.7, cruise 0.45/0.3, approach 0.6, landing reverse 1.0/1.0, landed 0.2.
- Island: `sol`; pursuit → `skandal` + `siren(true)`; escape/bust/bribe → back to the tune before
  the pursuit if it was a mission's (`vals`, `jul`), else the level tune (§7.2).
- **Every mission complete**: `audio.applause(2)` + `jingle('complete')` (the film's applause gag).

### 12.3 Sound effects (Phase 0 placeholders with these names; WP-H polishes)

| name | recipe |
|---|---|
| `chime()` | seatbelt "pling-plong": `tone(659,.5,'sine',.1)` + `tone(523,.8,'sine',.1,null,.4)` |
| `pling()` | call button: `tone(1300,.35,'sine',.12)`; since feature 59 also the reception's desk bell (§10.37) |
| `phone()` | the porter's desk phone ringing for the site manager (feature 59, §10.37): two trills 0.55 s apart, each ten 0.028 s square tones alternating 960 and 1180 Hz every 0.03 s |
| `dingdong()` | PA: 659 then 523 Hz sine, 0.45 s each |
| `beep()` | metal detector: 880 Hz square ×3 pulses |
| `applause(secs = 2)` | ~60 short band-passed noise bursts at random times over `secs` |
| `heartbeat()` | 55 Hz sine double thump |
| `rattle()` | `noise(0.3, 0.15, 300)` |
| `flush()` | noise sweep down 2 kHz → 300 Hz, 1.2 s |
| `squeak()` | fin pop: tone slide 900 → 1400 Hz, 0.12 s |
| `siren(on)` | two-tone 650/500 Hz square, alternating 0.45 s, gain 0.05 while on; `main.updateAudio` keeps it on while a pursuit runs or H is held in the borrowed jeep (feature 51, §10.34; that one at full loudness) |
| `laugh()` | crowd: 8 short formant-ish noise bursts |
| `knock()`, `slap()`, `doorSlam()` | short filtered noise thumps |
| `ambulance()` | distant two-tone 960/770 Hz sine fading in and out over 4 s |
| `baa()` | tone slide 420 → 300 Hz with vibrato |
| `oink()` | the grisbil's horn (feature 5, §10.9): two nasal grunts 0.22 s apart, each a 190 → 120 Hz sawtooth and a band-passed noise burst; `honk.update` plays it on H and every 0.75 s while H is held, and `updateAudio` keeps `horn` off in the grisbil |
| `woof(size = 1, n = 2, vol = 1)` | a watchdog (feature 31, §10.21): `n` barks 0.23 s apart, each a sawtooth (300–350 Hz ÷ `size`) jumping up 1.2× and falling to 0.55× in 0.15 s through a band-pass at 950 Hz ÷ `size`, with a band-passed noise breath; `size` the dog's (the poodle's 0.72 yaps higher), `vol` 0..1 for the distance |
| `whistle()` | a dog's owner whistling it home (feature 31, §10.21): a sine 1700 → 2400 Hz (0.14 s), then 2350 → 1500 Hz (0.36 s) |
| `flap(n = 1, vol = 1)` | a flock lifting (feature 43, §10.31): 3 + 2n (at most 12) wing claps 0.05 s apart, band-passed noise bursts of 0.05 s at 0.8–1.6 kHz, fading, over a 500 → 1700 Hz noise sweep of 0.25–0.57 s; `vol` 0..1 for the distance; `birds` plays it for the take-offs of each 0.15 s |
| `gull(vol = 1, low = 1)` | a gull's cry (feature 43, §10.31): two sawtooth glides through a band-pass at 1.9 kHz, 1150 → 1650 Hz (0.14 s) and, 0.17 s on, 1550 → 880 Hz (0.34 s); `low` scales every frequency, and under 0.6 adds a 0.4 s noise breath: the herons' croak at 0.32 |
| `thud()`, `crash()`, `coin()`, `pickup()` | existing |
| `toasterDown()`, `pop()` | a G17 toaster (feature 33, §10.24): the lever going down (a band-passed noise clack and a 170 → 110 Hz square), the bread popping up (a short 2.6 kHz noise burst and a 380 → 900 Hz sine) |
| `stamp()`, `stampFail()` | the stunt jumps' stamp (feature 40, §10.27): a rubber thump on paper (a 1.5 kHz noise slap, a 96 → 52 Hz sine, a low noise tail); UNDERKÄND adds a falling two-tone square buzz (196 → 98, 147 → 74 Hz) |
| `squirt()`, `splat()` | the sun cream (feature 35, §10.26): a squeeze of the bottle every 0.28 s while E is held (a 0.07 s band-passed noise at 0.9–1.2 kHz and a 240 → 170 Hz sine), too much landing on her back (a 0.22 s low-passed noise and a 1.4 kHz → 400 Hz sweep) |
| `splash(k = 0)` | water (existing at k 0: a band-passed noise burst and a sweep down); feature 24 (§10.20): `k` 0..2 lengthens, lowers and lifts it (`game.waterSplash`: 1 a fall from the 10 m tower, 1–2 a stomp's cannonball), and over 1 a 75 → 38 Hz sine boom under it |
| `pipHorn()` | a golf cart's horn (feature 74, §10.40): a short, feeble pip-pip, two 0.08 s square tones gliding 1245 → 1175 Hz 0.14 s apart with a faint octave; `golf.update` plays it on H and every 0.45 s while H is held, and `updateAudio` keeps `horn` off in a car whose spec has a `horn` |
| `engine(on, revs, load, electric = false, diesel = false)` | the motor loop (existing); `electric` (a golf cart, feature 74): a quiet hum, 150 + 420 × revs Hz through a low-pass at 500 + 1100 × revs, gain 0.008 + 0.01 × load; `diesel` (the tractor, feature 121, §10.54): a low putt-putt, 26 + 30 × revs Hz and its sub-octave through a low-pass at 200 + 360 × revs + 260 × load, gain 0.05 + 0.035 × load |
| `pip()` | Ole's calculator alarm (feature 30, §10.10): PIP-PIP-PIP twice, 2794 Hz square pips of 0.06 s 0.12 s apart, the second three 0.55 s on; the nap plays it twice |
| `whirr(secs = 1.2)` | Herr Storch's film camera (feature 6, §10.11): the clockwork motor, 18 soft clicks a second (0.016 s band-passed noise bursts at 2.6 kHz) over a faint 118 → 112 Hz sawtooth hum; when he films (2.1 s), on a viewfinder (1.2 s) and for the film night (2.4 s) |
| `shutter()` | Ole's camera (feature 47, §10.32): the flash's pop and the shutter's double click (band-passed noise bursts of 0.05 s at 2.6 kHz and, 0.06 s on, 0.03 s at 3.8 kHz), then the flash charging again, a faint sine rising 1800 → 5000 Hz over 0.9 s from 0.15 s; at "Si omelett!" with the white flash |
| `glide()` | feature 3 (§10.7), arms out: two soft band-passed noise sweeps up, 450 → 1500 Hz (0.7 s) and 900 → 2400 Hz (0.5 s, +0.15 s) |
| `jingle(kind)` | `start`, `complete`, `fail`, `pryl` (replaces `record`) |
| `trad(name)` | §12.1 |

## 13. Visual style and palette

### 13.1 Look

Keep the engine's toon/cel-shading, four-band ramp and ink outlines (`#1d1426`). Re-palette to a
**1979 charter brochure**: sun-bleached whitewash, terracotta, ochre, turquoise pools, palm greens,
orange 70s cabin seats, SunTrip yellow. Colour dramaturgy: grey snowy Arlanda → orange cabin →
cloud whiteout → blue above-cloud sky → hazy descent over the ocean → white-and-ochre island →
orange-violet grisfest night → sunset on Christmas Eve.

### 13.2 Material palette

| group | colours |
|---|---|
| cabin | seat `#D2601F`, antimacassar `#F2EFE6`, wall `#E6DCC4`, rack `#D8CDB4`, curtain `#1F4F55`, stewardess `#1E9AA0`, tray `#9A9A92`, sign red `#E0342A`, carpet `#5a4a3a` |
| plane | white `#F4F4F0`, cheat line `#1B2F6B`, sun `#F07A1E`, belly `#B8BEC6`, fin cap `#C8202A` |
| Arlanda 1976 | orange counters `#d8743a`, wood `#9a6a3a`, brown carpet `#6a4a32`, cream walls `#e8e0cc`, snow `#f2f4f6` |
| island | whitewash `#f4efe6`, terracotta `#c0623a`, ochre sand `#c9a26b`, beach sand `#e8cf98`, Monte Rojo `#a5532f` / `#c27a45`, bougainvillea `#c2307a`, palm `#3f7a3a`, butano `#f07a1e`, sea/pools `#1c7fb8`, SunTrip yellow `#f7c31b`, SunTrip red text `#d8321e`, Guardia green `#2e5e3e` |

### 13.3 Sky / fog / light palettes (fog colour = sky horizon = `body` background, always together)

`setSkyPalette({ top, horizon, fogNear, fogFar, sun, sunI, hemiSky, hemiGround, hemiI, sunDir, cloudRim })`.

**Cloud rim** (Phase 3 r2, optional field): the town clouds' outline colour (`MAT.cloudRim`, the
clouds' own `outlineMat(0.6, …)`). The island palettes set it: `day` `0x6f9ccc` (as before),
`night` `0x101433`, `sunset` `0xa0605a`. A fixed sky-blue rim glowed cyan round the dark night
clouds over the farm, the lighthouse and the race, and blue round the peach sunset clouds on the
julafton mantra and the Rio card; now night clouds get a dark ink-like line and sunset ones a warm
one. The flight palettes leave it out (the town clouds are hidden in the flight level).

| palette | top | horizon | fog near/far | sun / I | hemi sky / ground / I | cabin window |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gate` (flight: gate, takeoff) | `0x8e99a6` | `0xc7ccd2` | 40 / 300 | `0xdfe8f2` 0.8 | `0xc8d4e0` / `0xf0f4f8` 1.5 | `0xb8c0c8` |
| `clouds` (climb) | `0xe8eef4` | `0xf4f6f8` | 160 / 520 | `0xffffff` 1.0 | `0xffffff` / `0xe8eef4` 1.7 | `0xf8f8f8` |
| `above` (cruise) | `0x1f6fd0` | `0xbfe0ff` | 300 / 900 | `0xfff4dc` 2.6 | `0xe6f2ff` / `0xffffff` 1.6 | `0x7fb8ef` |
| `descent` (approach) | `0x2a86e0` | `0xf2e4c4` | 260 / 820 | `0xffe7b8` 2.8 | `0xd8ecff` / `0xa08060` 1.5 | `0x9ad0f0` |
| `island` (landing, landed; island `day`) | `0x2a86e0` | `0xf2e4c4` | 220 / 760 | `0xffe7b8` 2.9 | `0xd8ecff` / `0xa08060` 1.45 | `0xa8d8f8` |
| `night` (grisfest; free-roam nights, §10.10) | `0x141a3c` | `0x3a2f4e` | 120 / 600 | `0x9fb4ff` 0.9 | `0x5a6aa0` / `0x3a2a20` 0.9 | — |
| `sunset` (grisfest dusk, julafton mantra, Rio; free-roam evenings, §10.10) | `0x3a4fa0` | `0xf7a26b` | 200 / 760 | `0xffb070` 2.2 | `0xffd8b0` / `0x8a5a40` 1.3 | — |

Flight palettes keep `fogNear ≥ 40` so the interior is never fogged. Night: string lights are unlit
`MeshBasicMaterial` bulbs (grisfest block, Kasbah neon). Lit windows and lamps that glow only after
dark draw while `gfx.skyDark()`: by default while the sky `top` is dark (r + g + b < 0.8 in linear
light: `night` and `sunset`), and the lighthouse while `gfx.beaconLit()` (by default the sun weaker
than 1.6); the free-roam clock (feature 30, §10.10) forces both with `gfx.setNightLights(on)` while
it blends the island palettes between missions (lit 20:00–06:30), and `Game.setSky` hands them back
to the sky with `setNightLights(null)`. The hotels' windows
(hotels.js `nightMesh`) and, since Phase 3, the street lamps' lantern panes and star centres
(town.js `nightGlow`, one unlit mesh for the whole island; block builders may add their own night
lights to it in world coordinates while `buildTown` runs). The coast adds the marina's quay-lamp
globes and green harbour light and Gando's apron floodlight faces (each glow a centimetre larger
than the lit face, so they never z-fight). The lighthouse beam (night only) is additive light
fading from warm at the lantern to nothing at its 140 m end, unfogged and outer faces only (Phase 3:
plain alpha read as a grey tube with a disc on its end).

**Sun direction** (Phase 3): the island palettes carry `sunDir`, the sun's offset from the point
`followSun` tracks (+z = south): `day` and `night` `[70, 130, 45]` (high, from the ESE, as before),
`sunset` `[-105, 60, 60]` (low, ≈ 26°, from the WSW: 28° N in December), so the julafton mantra and
the Rio card get long shadows pointing away from the sunset instead of short noon shadows towards
it. The flight palettes have none and keep the default `[70, 130, 45]`; every island palette sets
it, so switching back restores it. The 150 m shadow frustum holds the long shadows.

### 13.4 CSS tokens (style.css; WP-H)

Keep `--ink #1d1426`, `--cream #fff8e6`, `--yellow #ffd23f`. Replace purple/pink with `--sun
#f7c31b`, `--orange #f07a1e`, `--sea #1c7fb8`, `--teal #1e9aa0`, `--terracotta #c0623a`,
`--sand #e8cf98`. Meter fills: `.fear` `linear-gradient(90deg, #6ab0e8, #e0342a)`, `.skandal`
`linear-gradient(90deg, #f7c31b, #d8321e)` (as shipped by WP-H, each with a middle stop for a
richer ramp: `.fear` `#6ab0e8, #b070c0 60%, #e0342a`, `.skandal` `sun, orange 55%, red`; same end
colours, gradient over the whole bar). `body.fear-hot` adds a pulsing red vignette.
Pause card `--sea`. Big-map/minimap outside fill sand `#d9bf86`. Icons: `.pryl-icon` (a watch),
`.fen-icon` (a fin). Banner cls `skandal` replaces `shame`; add cls `fear`.

### 14.2 Init order and frame order (main.js, Phase 0)

Init: `initGfx` → `input.init` → `hud.init` → `fx.init` → fonts (Luckiest Guy ≤ 2.5 s) →
`buildTown(scene)` (calls `registerIslandLandmarks()` first, then `streets`, every block via
`BLOCK_BUILDERS[MAP[j][i]]`, `outskirts`, ped loops) → `this.cabin = buildCabin(scene, this)` →
`buildRioCard(scene)` (if present) → `finalizeProps(scene)` → `initCoins(scene)` →
`hud.buildBaseMap()` → `placeWorldCoins()` → `this.cabin.placeCoins()` → parked cars (the toys, the golf
carts and the tractor, last: feature 74, 121) → traffic (20)
→ peds (34) → NPC `Character`s (one per `CHARS` key except `stig`, the radio-only keys `levander
kapten pa guardia pax telefonist` and the cabin-owned `vardinna2`; `key` field; hidden until placed, §2.3) →
player `Character(CHARS.stig)` (`key = 'stig'`) → collectibles (`COLLECTIBLES`) → markers → `Shame`
→ `MissionRunner` → `BerraJob` (feature 2, §10.6) → `Glide` (feature 3, §10.7) → `PoolJudges` (feature 4, §10.8) → `DiveTower` (feature 24, §10.20; registers the ladder's two interactables, sets `DIVE_TOWER.live`) → `Honk` (feature 5, §10.9) → `DayClock` (feature 30, §10.10; registers the bed's interactable) → `StorchFilm` (feature 6, §10.11; registers Herr Storch's interactable, reads its stills) → `Eslov` (feature 7, §10.12; registers the rollerskier's interactable) → `PoolFest` (feature 8, §10.13) → `StigSorry` (feature 11, §10.14) → `PigTruck` (feature 15, §10.15) → `BaggageBelt` (feature 25, §10.16) → `Lapplisa` (feature 20, §10.17) → `GrisfestFree` (feature 21, §10.18; registers the gate's and the tourists' interactables) → `FruitStands` (feature 28, §10.19) → `Dogs` (feature 31, §10.21) → `Bathers` (feature 32, §10.22; registers the wake's interactable) → `SuntripShop` (feature 34, §10.23; registers the four wares' and the bag's interactables, sets `SUNTRIP_SHOP.live`) → `Toasters` (feature 33, §10.24; registers the seven toasters' interactables) → `LostBags` (feature 116, §10.52; notes each suitcase's home, registers the counter's interactable) → `Room107` (feature 38, §10.25; registers room 107's three interactables) → `Solkram` (feature 35, §10.26; registers Majsan's interactable) → `Stunts` (feature 40, §10.27) → `GangTalk` (feature 39, §10.28) → `RoofJump` (feature 41, §10.29; registers the three stair doors, sets `ROOF_JUMP.live`, places the roof coins) → `Mic` (feature 44, §10.30; registers the mic's interactable) → `Birds` (feature 43, §10.31; builds the four kinds' instanced meshes and puts every bird on its spot) → `Gags` (feature 47, §10.32; registers the two gags' interactables) → `BeachDream` (feature 57, §10.33; builds the towel and the foam, registers the towel's interactable) → `GuardiaJeep` (feature 51, §10.34) → `Lighthouse` (feature 52, §10.35; registers the two doors' interactables) → `ReceptionBell` (feature 59, §10.37; builds the bell, the card and the three suitcases with their solids, registers the bell's interactable) → `StreetRace` (feature 69, §10.38; registers José's and the chalkboard's interactables) → `GolfCarts` (feature 74, §10.40) → `BoatTrip` (feature 76, §10.41; builds the fin, registers the kiosk's interactable) → `Residents` (feature 77, §10.42) → `PhoneBooth` (feature 80, §10.43; registers booth 2's interactable) → `PoolBar` (feature 84, §10.44; registers the counter's and Fru Storch's interactables) → `Fishing` (feature 107, §10.45; builds the rod, its holder, the bucket, the float, the line and the four catches, registers the spot's interactable) → `MarketRoofs` (feature 92, §10.46; places the market's coin trail) → `Hitch` (feature 106, §10.47; registers the two spots' interactables) → `Binoculars` (feature 108, §10.48; builds the pair on the railing, registers the platform's interactable) → `Packhus` (feature 109, §10.49; builds the foreman, hidden, registers his interactable; the belt, its bins and the workers wait for the first shift) → `Volley` (feature 111, §10.50; builds the ball, its shadow and the landing ring, registers the ball's interactable) → `TouristPhoto` (feature 110, §10.51; registers the couple's interactable; the couple is made at its first show) → `Guagua` (feature 112, §10.53; registers the 13 stops' and the door's interactables) → `Traktor` (feature 121, §10.54; the farmer's `Character`, hidden) → `CamRig` → `load()` → `setLevel(levelFor(index), {instant:true})` →
`placeNpcs(true)` → spawn the player → portraits for every key in `CAST` (`renderPortrait`
restores each model's parent and transform, so seated cast members stay in their seats) →
`applySaveToWorld()` →
loop → `window.__ready = true` → `start()` in test mode.

Frame (`update`): hooks → one-shots (incl. E/J/R while seated) → fixed steps (player intent incl.
mantra/hold and the sprint × `bar.sprintK()` (feature 84), AI, cars (a landing calls `onCarAirEnd`, feature 40), `golf.step` (feature 74), people (`glide.step` → `skis.step`, feature 71 → the player's step → `glide.after` → `skis.after`, feature 3, 71 →
`belt.carry`, feature 25 → the NPCs → `party.step`, feature 21 → `bathers.step`, feature 32 → `mic.step`, feature 44 → `bell.step`, feature 59 → `packhus.step`, feature 109 → `volley.step`, feature 111 → `kort.step`, feature 110 → `traktor.step`, feature 121; in the
tourist couple's viewfinder the frozen branch takes Stig's walk from `kort.wish()`) —
traffic/peds skipped when `!levelDef.sim.*`) → `syncAll` (also
writes `ch.x/y/z` from `car.seatWorld(ch.seatSide)` for every car-seated character, player
included, so framing, bubbles and distance checks see where they really are) → `missions.update` →
`missions.updateFailed` → `shame.update` → `berraJob.update` (feature 2) → `glide.update` (feature 3) → `judges.update` (feature 4) → `tower.update` (feature 24) → `honk.update` (feature 5) → `day.update` (feature 30) → `film.update` (feature 6) → `eslov.update` (feature 7) → `skis.update` (feature 71) → `fest.update` (feature 8) → `sorry.update` (feature 11) → `pigs.update` (feature 15) → `belt.update` (feature 25) → `lapp.update` (feature 20) → `party.update` (feature 21) → `stands.update` (feature 28) → `dogs.update` (feature 31) → `bathers.update` (feature 32) → `shop.update` (feature 34) → `toasters.update` (feature 33) → `bags.update` (feature 116) → `room107.update` (feature 38) → `solkram.update` (feature 35) → `stunts.update` (feature 40) → `chat.update` (feature 39) → `roofs.update` (feature 41) → `mic.update` (feature 44) → `birds.update` (feature 43) → `dream.update` (feature 57) → `jeep.update` (feature 51) → `fyren.update` (feature 52) → `bell.update` (feature 59) → `gatlopp.update` (feature 69) → `golf.update` (feature 74) → `battur.update` (feature 76) → `residents.update` (feature 77) → `hytt.update` (feature 80) → `bar.update` (feature 84) → `fiske.update` (feature 107) → `awnings.update` (feature 92) → `hitch.update` (feature 106) → `kikare.update` (feature 108) → `packhus.update` (feature 109) → `volley.update` (feature 111) → `kort.update` (feature 110) → `guagua.update` (feature 112) → `traktor.update` (feature 121; after `syncAll`, so its jolts go on top of the car's synced tilt) → `cabin.tick(dt·timeScale, t, game)` (flight only) →
pickups/collectibles → props → `fx.tick` → `tickTown` → markers → camera → sun/sky → HUD → audio →
traffic recycling (island) → autosave. `loop` then renders, and when `film.grabNow` is set calls
`film.grab()` in the same task (Herr Storch's still from the frame's buffer, feature 6, §10.11), and when
`kort.grabNow` is set `kort.grab()` (the tourist couple's picture, the frame's part of the buffer, feature
110, §10.51).

### 14.3 Game API (main.js; Phase 0; **the contract every agent codes against**)

```js
// ---- state ----
game.level; game.levelDef; game.timeScale;            // §4.4
game.cabin;                                           // cabin object (§14.7)
game.player;  game.npcs[key];  game.cars;  game.named[name];
game.coins;                                           // pesetas
game.collected = { prylar: Set, fenor: Set, brodrostar: Set, vaskor: Set };  game.unlocked: Set;   // one Set per COLLECTIBLES set
game.holding;      // bool: Space held in flight (set in fixedStep)
game.mantraOn;     // bool: mantra currently held (after wind-up)
game.mantraMode;   // bool: island J = mantra (mantra stage)
game.carrying;     // null | { item } | { who } (the free-roam Berra job's { who: 'berra', job }, §10.6;
                   // a pig over his head { who: 'gris', job: 'pigs' }, §10.15; a lost suitcase on his
                   // head { item: 'vaska', bag }, §10.52: the idle giver can still be talked to)
game.stomping;     // bool: a stomp is on its way down (onLand slams); the glide clears it (§10.7)
game.glide;        // Glide (feature 3, §10.7): the free-roam glide after julafton
game.judges;       // PoolJudges (feature 4, §10.8): the sisters judge his dives at Flamenco's pool
game.tower;        // DiveTower (feature 24, §10.20): the 10 m diving tower at Flamenco's pool; tower.live,
                   // canClimb(), climb(up), put(up), dive, fromTop, radioSaid, last, climbs
game.records;      // { simhopp?: n, eslov?: s, solkram?: n, eslovSkidor?: s, … } free-roam bests, saved (§10.5)
game.honk;         // Honk (feature 5, §10.9): the island hears the horn in free roam
game.hornAt;       // null | { x, z, yaw, t, pigs }: the last free-roam horn press (§10.9)
game.day;          // DayClock (feature 30, §10.10): day.h (Spanish time, 0–24), day.run (moves by
                   // itself; false in test mode), day.set(h), day.resync(), day.dark, day.lit(),
                   // day.lineOk(text), async day.toMorning() (runner.begin), day.napping, day.last
game.film;         // StorchFilm (feature 6, §10.11): Herr Storch films Stig's tricks in free roam,
                   // his viewfinder, the stills and the film night after the end
game.eslov;        // Eslov (feature 7, §10.12): the rollerskier in free roam, the horn, Eslövloppet
game.skis;         // Rollerskis (feature 71, §10.39): Stig on the rollerskier's skis after the bodega;
                   // skis.on, v, yaw, surf, mode, fallen, falls, trial, runs, canLend(), waiting(),
                   // lend(), giveBack(kind), step(h), after(), update(dt), fall(kind), startTrial(),
                   // objective(), target(), markers(), auto (tests), last, cfg (SKIDOR)
game.fest;         // PoolFest (feature 8, §10.13): Små grodorna in Flamenco's pool after the end;
                   // fest.joined (Stig in the ring: handleOneShots gives Space to fest.hop(), no kick;
                   // fixedStep zeroes his wish), fest.posed(key), fest.visit, fest.phase, fest.last
game.sorry;        // StigSorry (feature 11, §10.14): Stig says sorry in free roam
game.pigs;         // PigTruck (feature 15, §10.15): the grisbil's pigs tumble off in free roam,
                   // the catch, the pen at the farm; pigs.jolt(car, 'land' | 'crash', impact) from
                   // onCarLanded / onCarImpact (the player's car)
game.belt;         // BaggageBelt (feature 25, §10.16): the baggage belt at Gando carries Stig in free
                   // roam; belt.seated (on a bag: handleOneShots gives Space to standUp('hop') and E to
                   // standUp('off'), R calls release(false) first, updateHud shows its prompt)
                   // fest.joined (Stig in the ring: handleOneShots gives Space to fest.hop(), no kick;
                   // fixedStep zeroes his wish), fest.posed(key), fest.visit, fest.phase, fest.last
game.lapp;         // Lapplisa (feature 20, §10.17): Majsan tickets a car left on the sidewalk and has
                   // it towed, Angerud's hire car and the film's first meeting, her praise for a car
                   // straight in a Flamenco bay; lapp.posed(key) (syncAll), lapp.owns(key) (honk.free)
game.party;        // GrisfestFree (feature 21, §10.18): the grisfest's evening for 800 pesetas at the

                   // back), backSpot(car), step(h), update(dt), home(), fetch(), takes, chases, bumps, honks,
                   // spills, fetched, puffs, joltMax, last, log, cfg (TRAKTORN)
game.npcPosed(key) -> bool   // an NPC held in a pose of its own: §9.4 idleAnim or a free-roam module's
                   // (berraJob, judges, film, eslov, fest, lapp, party, stands, mic, birds, gags, dream, bell, gatlopp, bar, volley); syncAll gives it no
                   // wave, turn or chatter, and the gang's talk leaves it be (§10.28)
game.bathers;      // Bathers (feature 32, §10.22): tourists on the sun loungers, Berra and Robban fried;
                   // bathers.loose (the bathers off their loungers: allChars, areaHit), step(h)
                   // (fixedStep), onPropBroken(p, vx, vz) (from onPropBroken, after the lounger's own
                   // SKANDAL), onGetUp(ch) (onGetUp: true for a bather, his line said), scare(x, z, r,
                   // flee) (the shark warning, feature 44, §10.30), held, last
game.shop;         // SuntripShop (feature 34, §10.23): SunTrip-butiken in free roam; shop.live,
                   // dress(def, name) (setPlayerOutfit: his bought look over the outfit), worn,
                   // owned, off, trapp, trappT, bag, clerk, saveData()/loadData(s) (save's `shop`), last
game.breakProp(p, vx, vz, car) -> p | null   // car.js's smash: null when refused (a fruit stall
                   // outside free roam or under any car but his: the car meets a wall); Stig's sorry
                   // ('stand' for a fruit stall), then stands.onBroken (feature 28)
game.outfitOverrides; // { key: outfit } from UNLOCKS[name].outfit, merged over the island set by applyOutfits (§10.3)
game.witnessOverride; // null | UNLOCKS[name].witness, merged over the witness rule's config on the island (§7.2)
game.onBounce(ch, b);   // Character.step: ch bounced on trampoline block b (the boing; the judges, §10.8; film.trick('studs'))
game.onLand(ch, v, y);  // Character.step: ch landed at v m/s (> 6) on floor height y (tower.onLand(v, y) and
                        // roofs.onLand(v, y), feature 41, then the judges; film.onLand; any other landing in
                        // water waterSplash's for the dust; the stomp)
game.waterSplash(x, z, v, bomb = false);   // water thrown up by a hard landing at v m/s in a pool or pond: the
                        // drops (fx.splash) and audio.splash(k) grow with k = (v − 6) / 16 (clamped 0..1); a
                        // bomb (a stomp) adds a column and a boom and shakes the camera to 0.6 + 0.8 k (feature 24)
game.bumpedT;      // > 0 for 0.4 s after a trolley bowl / turbulence fall
game.inDialog;  game.autoDialog;  game.dialogSpeed (55, TEST 220);
game.closure;      // null | a race's closed course { nodes: Set<nodeId>, update(), closed(nodeId) }
                   // (Phase 2 gate; set by race init, cleared by its cleanup; §9.2 race)

// ---- levels ----
game.levelFor(index) -> 'flight' | 'island'
game.setLevel(name, { index, instant = true } = {})
async game.transitionTo(name)
game.restoreAmbience()                    // level tune, mantraMode=false; island palette (and
                                          // day.resync(), §10.10); flight:
                                          // cabin.stopTurbulence() (Phase 2), then
                                          // setPhase(phaseForIndex(index), {instant}) no hold,
                                          // seatbelt off, palette + map for it (§9.4 item 6)
game.levelTune() -> name                  // review fix 1: the level's ambient tune (flight `muzak`;
                                          // island game.islandTune). Everything that reverts the
                                          // music uses it (setLevel, restoreAmbience, shame.endPursuit
                                          // unless a mission's tune played before, grisfest onEnd)
game.islandTune                           // 'sol' | 'samba' (saved as `tune`, §10.5)
game.setIslandTune(name)                  // switches now only if the island's ambient tune is
                                          // playing (never over `skandal` or a music cue); saves
game.cycleMusic() -> label;  game.musicLabel()   // pause-menu Musik: på → samba (after the
                                          // unlock) → av → på (§11.3)
game.setSky(name)                         // island palettes: 'day' | 'night' | 'sunset'; also
                                          // setNightLights(null): the lights follow the sky (§13.3)

// ---- NPCs ----
game.npc(key)                             // 'stig' → player
game.charDef(key)                         // CHARS[key]
game.placeNpc(key, lm, dx = 0, dz = 0, yaw?)   // unseat first (car: g.unseat(ch); plane seat:
                                          // cabin.unseatCharacter(ch)), then teleport, show,
                                          // busy = true until placeNpcs(true); key 'stig' = player
game.hideNpc(key);  game.showNpc(key)     // hideNpc unseats first too
game.placeNpcs(force = false)             // §4.5; force also re-applies levelDef.outfits(g)
                                          // (applyOutfits) except during an outro (§10.4)
game.setNpcOutfit(key, name);  game.setPlayerOutfit(name)   // re-render portraits
game.stomp()       // feature 3: J in the air (vy −18, stomping, the kick sound); the glide's tap calls it
game.say(target, text, secs = 2);  game.radio(who, text)   // say: at least 1 + 0.045 s a character
                                          // (halved in test mode; Phase 3, §11.4); an empty text or
                                          // secs <= 0 is an unsay
game.unsay(target)                        // takes target's bubble down now (hud.unsay); saying(t)
                                          // false, sayEnd back to the bubbles still up (Phase 3)
game.bark(ch, kind) -> text               // kind ouch | getUp | kicked | carjack: a line from the
                                          // speaker's table (Ole / local / Swedish; §14.10, r2)
npc.steer?(h) -> { x, z } | null          // feature 2: a free-roam module walking an NPC; fixedStep
                                          // sets the NPC's wish (m/s) from it, else 0 (§10.6)

// ---- flight seats ----
game.sitPlayer(seatId) -> bool            // via cabin.seatCharacter; sets player.seatId
game.standPlayer()                        // to the seat's aisle spot; player.seatId = null

// ---- interactables ----
game.addInteractable({ id, x, z, y = 0.15, pos?(g) -> { x, z, y? }, r = 1.2, prompt, priority = 0,
                       whileSeated = false, skis = false, enabled?(g), use(g) }) -> remove()
// pos (if given) is evaluated every frame and overrides x/z/y (moving anchors such as the trolley).
// skis: offered while Stig is on the borrowed rollerskis (feature 71, §10.39); on them no other
// interactable and no gang talk is (a mission's giver and the cars still are).
// nearestInteractable order, standing: interactables with priority ≥ 100 (haggle bid) > mission
// giver talk (idle, < 3.4 m, not while game.carrying: feature 2, §10.6) > other interactables (enabled, in range) by priority then distance >
// the gang's talk ({ type: 'chat', who }: chat.nearest(), < 3.0 m, free roam on the island, §10.28) >
// cars (if verbs.enterCars and !car.noEnter and !locked shown as prompt).
// Seated: whileSeated interactables by priority then distance > 'stand' (unless the stage has
// lockSeat). Giver talk is never offered while seated (stand up first).

// ---- cars and riders ----
game.ensureNamedCar(name);  game.spawnMissionCar(m, type, x, z, yaw, opts)
game.seat(ch, car, side);  game.unseat(ch, x?, z?)          // existing
car.seatWorld(side) -> { x, y, z }                           // Phase 0 (car.js): world seat position
car.seatAt(side) -> { x, z }                                 // feature 121 (car.js): a seat's car-local spot (spec `seat`, else the old ones)
game.addRider(defKey, car, slot = 'rear') -> Object3D        // decorative bust; slots 'rear' | 'bed' | 'window1..4'
game.removeRiders(car)
game.removeRiderOf(key)                  // Phase 0b: drop that character's rider busts (placeNpc/showNpc call it)
game.speedCap                            // Phase 0b: null | m/s cap on walk/sprint (carry); sprint off while set

// ---- cinematics / dialogue / cues ----
game.cinematic(a, b);  game.cinematicOne(a);  game.endCinematic()
game.cutTo(spec);  game.endCut()          // spec = lm name | { at, dist, height } ; camera only
game.inCutaway -> bool                    // Polish: true while a cutaway camera is active (cutTo,
                                          // a `cut` cue, a scene `cam`, a cutTo outroCam) until
                                          // endCut/endCinematic. shame.js (WP-H) defers PANIK
                                          // while it is true
async game.dialog(lines)                  // lines: [who, text, cue?]
game.cue(c)                               // §9.3
game.wait(secs)

// ---- money / unlocks / end ----
async game.pay(n) -> true                 // Ole pays if short (§10.2)
game.addCoins(n)                          // negative allowed, floors at 0
game.unlock(name, { holdToast }?) -> held toast | null   // UNLOCKS[name] (§10.3)
async game.playEndCard()                  // §11.7: the Rio cinematic (wired in Phase 2), then
                                          // back at flamencoPool with the completion banner

// ---- meter hooks ----
game.onPanicIdle()                        // §5.9
game.interruptMantra()                    // jolts and fear cues: a held mantra restarts its wind-up (0.6 s)
game.frozenT                              // > 0 while frozen (bust freeze); input ignored (R too)
// Frozen player car (inDialog, mission 'failed', frozenT, PANIK, or game.freezeCar: the race
// countdown): brake only while rolling forward (car.js reads brake at < 0.5 m/s as reverse),
// handbrake on, so it stops and holds. Phase 3 r2: brake 1 crept every car but the bus backwards
// to −0.35 × top speed, 22 m back off the race grid by "KÖR!".

// ---- collectibles ----
game.collectibles[set] -> [Collectible]   // built from COLLECTIBLES (§10.1) at their landmarks
game.collect(set, c)  // +250, the set's jingle/splash/sparkle, the collect card, the radio, 7/7, save;
                      // a `keep` set's c is marked (c.mark()), the others' removed (feature 33)
game.dressRoom107()   // worldHooks.rum107(collected, unlocked): room 107 shows what is found (feature 38,
                      // §10.25); called by collect, unlock and applySaveToWorld

// ---- map ----
game.mapMarkers(all);  game.mapLabels();  game.mapLegend() -> html

// ---- tests ----
game.debugWarp(x, z, yaw)                 // stands up first if seated, off a hitch truck (§10.47), the binoculars down (§10.48), off the packing shed's belt (§10.49), a volleyball match off (§10.50), the tourist couple's camera down (§10.51), off the guagua (§10.53); snapNext
game.approachSpot(lm) -> { x, z, yaw }    // §4.4 spawn rule (landmark + 1.5 m facing back, else the landmark)
game.freeSpot(cx, cz, rMin, rMax, ok?) -> { x, z }   // random free ground spot; ok(x, z) filters (Phase 2)
game.footReach(cx, cz, R) -> (x, z) => bool   // on-foot flood fill (0.5 m grid, 0.45 m step, no jumps; Phase 2)
game.lmOffset(lm, dx, dz) -> { x, z, yaw }   // a HOMES-style offset from a landmark
game.unseatAny(ch)                        // off a car seat or a plane seat
game.testMode                             // ?test=1
window.__game, __lm(name), __props, __stats(), __ready, __frame
```

Hard-coded Bigmouth names removed: `'nick'` (→ `PLAYER_KEY = 'stig'`), the `cleanupMission` key
list, `got.records/mosquitoes`, `spawnMuscle`, `'hydrant'`/`'pump'` special cases, `isHearse`
(→ `isPursuer`), the "Hey Nick." fallback, `BRIDGETON COMPLETE!`, `resetToRoad` literals 80/280.

### 14.4 gfx.js (Phase 0)

```js
export function setSkyPalette({ top, horizon, fogNear, fogFar, sun, sunI, hemiSky, hemiGround, hemiI, sunDir, cloudRim })
  // sky uniforms (sky material stashed as MAT.sky), scene.fog colour/near/far, document.body bg,
  // sun colour/intensity, hemi colours/intensity, sunDir [x, y, z] = the sun's offset from the
  // followSun point (Phase 3, §13.3), cloudRim = the town clouds' outline colour (MAT.cloudRim;
  // Phase 3 r2, §13.3). Missing fields keep their value.
export function setCloudsVisible(on)     // MAT._clouds.visible
export function setShadows(on)           // sun.castShadow
export function signMesh(text, w, h, opts) -> Mesh   // opts.double (Polish): adds a child plane
  // turned π about Y with the same material, so the text reads unmirrored from both sides (each
  // plane FrontSide). Callers position/rotate the returned mesh as before.
// MAT.water retinted 0x1c7fb8 (sea and pools). tickSky unchanged (clouds hidden in flight).
```

### 14.5 camera.js (Phase 0; WP-A1 may tune)

```js
cam.profile = null | { pivotH, dist, pitchMin, pitchMax, pitch0, noPull, fov, cineSide, cineUp, clampZ? }
cam.clampActive = bool     // set each frame by main: flight level && cabin.inCabin(focus); then the eye z
                           // is clamped to profile.clampZ and pitch steepens (§5.3)
cam.openFloor = bool       // set each frame by main: the gate lounge (§5.3); frame/frameOne then use the
                           // Bigmouth framing despite the profile (cine.open: fov 50)
cam.setProfile(p)          // sets profile, snaps pitch to p.pitch0, snapNext; null = Bigmouth
cam.frame(a, b)            // profile-aware (§5.3); two people < 0.3 m apart: from in front of a
cam.frameOne(a)            // single-target framing (both modes)
cam.cutTo({ x, y, z }, { x, y, z })   // cine pos/look; release() returns
cam.scope = null | { pos: Vector3, yaw, pitch, fov }   // the lifeguard's binoculars (feature 108, §10.48)
                           // and the tourist couple's camera (feature 110, §10.51):
                           // set, it is the view: the eye exactly at pos, looking along yaw and pitch
                           // (+ up) at fov, no easing, before any cine; its owner moves it every frame
                           // and sets it null (and cam.fov to the next view's) when they come down
// on-foot branch: pivotH/dist/fov from profile; pitch clamped to [pitchMin, pitchMax] in both the
// mouse branch and every frame; pull-in skipped when noPull.
```

**Pull-in** (Phase 3; on foot and in cars, no `noPull` profile): the pivot→eye sight line is
tested with `segmentBlocked(…, 'prop', 0.25)` (0.25 m samples; at 0.8 m palm trunks and poles were
missed) and the eye stops 0.45 m (level) short of the first sample inside a solid, but never
closer than `ARM` 1.6 m. With less level room than that arm allows at the current pitch (his back
to a wall), the eye **climbs** on the 1.6 m arm (`pitch = acos(room / 1.6)`); past `CAP` 1.25 rad
it stays at that angle, moves in over the head (level offset = the room, ≥ 0.05 m) and looks
further ahead instead (as the cabin `clampPitch`). Until Phase 3 the 1.6 m floor put the eye
inside the wall (a one-colour frame at 2.4–8.9 % of standable spots × 8 headings in the hotel and
centre blocks); a sweep of the real rig over the same spots finds 0. Bushes and other `prop`
solids stay see-through by design. **Stand-off disc** (Phase 3 r2, both modes): the eye then keeps
`EYE_R` 0.45 m off every solid's face (`discPush` with top ≥ the eye − 0.3), not only along the
sight line: met at a slant the line's 0.45 m left it 0.05–0.3 m from the wall, inside façade relief
(Flamenco's piers 0.31 m, the band 0.21 m, window boxes 0.42 m). It is pushed out; if a solid then
stands between it and the pivot (a corner), it is pulled in along the sight line until the disc is
clear. **Camera ceilings** (§14.7) keep the eye out of registered overhangs, on foot and (Phase 3
r2) in cars. **Side slide** (Phase 3 r2, on foot; continuous since r3): his back to a wall under a
low ceiling, the capped climb left the eye 0.35–0.6 m over his head (a top-down view of his
shoulders), and a capped eye 1.6–2.6 m out sat against his back with his head cut off. When a
ceiling caps the eye or hangs within 0.5 m above it (`ceilingOver`, grown 0.3 m) and the eye is
nearer the pivot than `SIDE` 2.6 m, the eye's target is a slide along the wall to `SIDE` from the
pivot (the side it is on; tested at 0.25 m with the 0.45 m stand-off; no slide with less than 0.3 m
of room), and down to 0.6 m above the pivot only as far as that keeps it no nearer than before: a
three-quarter view of him with the way ahead (at 1.5–1.9 m he filled the frame). **The side** is kept
`SLIDE_HOLD` 0.3 s (`cam.slideT`, from when the slide took it) before the other side may take over
with `SLIDE_HYST` 0.5 m more room; sooner only when this side has collapsed and the other has more
room: 0.3 m or less, or cut this frame by more than `SLIDE_CUT` 0.2 m (a room sample) so far that the
slid eye would come within `NEAR` 1.2 m (level) of the pivot, with `SLIDE_HYST`/2 more room on the
other side (r3 repair2: without the hold the eye cut from shoulder to shoulder 4 frames apart in the
1.3 m slot by the friskotek's notice board; on any cut by 0.5 m it cut 3 m to the other shoulder for
0.1 m more room). The slide is a lateral offset kept in the rig (`cam.slide`, + = his right), eased
towards its target within one side, out at `SLIDE_K` 6/s (towards 0 once no ceiling is near or the
eye is `SIDE` out) and in at `SLIDE_IN` 12/s (the eye starts out close over his head), and cut each
frame to the room each side has; it is 0 in cars, with a profile and after a snap. Four cases are
cuts (the slide goes straight to its target and the eye snaps with it): a **swap of sides** (eased
through 0, the eye passed through his head as the camera turned under a low ceiling with a wall
near: r3 repair); a slide that **starts** (under 0.3 m) **as the eye is cut in** by more than 1 m
relative to him (`cam.lpx/lpy/lpz`, last frame's pivot; a pole pulls it in as the camera turns, or a
canopy starts to cap it and drops it: the eye jumps anyway, and eased in it sat over his head for a
frame or two); a slide that, eased, **would hold the eye within `CLOSE`** 1.0 m of the pivot where
its target would not (r3 repair2: strafing under the bungalow awning the cap dropped the eye 0.95 m
and the eased slide held it 0.72 m from his head; not at `NEAR`: walking under a balcony row with the
eye 1.1–1.2 m over his head that turned the ease into a 2.6 m sideways cut); and a **wedged** eye:
0.1 m or more behind the pivot with so little room to either side that the slid eye would stay
nearer than `ARM` (his back in a corner: the back of the fold between its wall and crag 1's end),
when a slide measured from the pivot itself (beside him) takes it further out, to the side with more
room. Once wedged (`cam.wedged`, `cam.wedgeT`) it stays so for `SLIDE_HOLD` and then until the slid
eye would be `ARM` + 0.3 m out, and keeps its side unless the other has `SLIDE_HYST` more room or this
one 0.3 m or less (r3 repair2: the room is sampled every 0.25 m, and the bare test toggled as the
camera turned under the fold's shelter, 3–4 cuts out to the side view and back per turn; a 0.3 m
band alone still let a slow turn in and out twice, as the pull-in's 0.25 m steps moved the eye's
base). Until r3 it was all or nothing (only
nearer than `ARM` − 0.05) and every frame with a wall behind snapped the eye: walking out from under
a porch, the eye jumped 2.2–2.7 m in one frame (141 of 606 real-input walks under the island's
ceilings). Every pull-in or push snaps the eye (no
damping lag into the wall) — in height only downwards: a ceiling that stops capping lets the eye
rise at the damped rate (9.8/s). **Dialogue framing** (`frame`, `frameOne` without a profile): the side whose sight line is
clear; when both are blocked, the side with more room, the eye 0.45 m short of the solid (≥ 1.6 m
out) instead of inside a house (fataga's 13 m two-shot).

### 14.6 Actors (Phase 0 minimal; WP-E owns afterwards)

**models.js**
```js
export const CHARS = { stig: {...}, ... };         // keys = Appendix A; Phase 0: approximate looks
export const CAST = Object.keys(CHARS).filter((k) => CHARS[k].portrait !== false);
export function buildCharacter(def), animateCharacter(m, st, dt), randomPed(r, { flight } = {}), buildBust(def)
export function buildBustGeo(def) -> BufferGeometry   // merged bust, origin at torso bottom, +z forward
// randomPed(r, { flight: true }): Swedish charter passengers only (no locals) for the cabin, lounge,
//   walkers and stowers; a ped def has `local: bool` (Spanish local, ~30 % on the island). Random
//   sequences changed in WP-E (the shorts draw follows the dress draw), and buildBust/buildBustGeo
//   drop a random ped's sunhat or bucket hat. buildBust(def).userData.h = the bust's height (seat fit).
//   The model has m.legLen and m.headTop (= m.height).
export function outfitDef(key, outfit) -> def         // { ...CHARS[key], ...CHARS[key].outfits?.[outfit] }
```
New def fields (WP-E implements; unknown fields are ignored until then): `hat`
(`'trilby' | 'pilot' | 'tricorn' | 'bucket' | 'sunhat' | 'tomte' | 'scarf' | 'cap'`; `'cap'` as a
hat on top of hair; its colour is `hatC`, Phase 0a), `dress` (colour; cone skirt), `shades` (colour; filled lenses), `beard`,
`print: [c1, c2, c3]` (confetti blobs on the torso), `tuft`, `tie`, `bowtie`, `vest`, `held`
(`'camera' | 'boombox' | 'accordion' | 'congas' | 'cup' | 'mirror' | 'broom' | 'giraffe' |
'butterKnife' | 'knacke' | 'handbag'`), hair `'page'`, `hairFlower`, `ring` (css), `outfits`, `portrait`.
A held `'broom'` is lifted so that its bristles stop at his soles, the hand sliding down the handle
(feature 77, §10.42: hanging from the hand they went 0.2 m into the floor, through a balcony's slab).
WP-E added (full list in the models.js header): `capStyle`, `printStyle` (`confetti | dots | floral |
check`), `stripe`/`stripes`, `sash`, `scarf` (neck), `apron`, `belly`, `collar`, `suit` (shirt colour
in the jacket's V), `coat`, `epaulets`, `badge`, `chain`, `belt`, `pinafore`, `shorts`/`baggy`,
`legsC`, `hands`, `glassesBig`, `lens`, `aviator`, `lashes`, `curlySides`, `thin`, `sideburns`, `nose`
shapes. Phase 3: `skirtPrint` (the dress's dots, else `print`), `mittenBand`, `shortsHem`, `peakC`
(a cap's peak), hat `'fur'`. Feature 7: `bib` (text printed on a single `stripe`'s front, the band
then 0.2 × torso high: the rollerskier's `ESLÖV`, #1b3a8a on a transparent canvas, an unlit strip of
the band's elliptic cylinder 1.9 rad round the front, no outline; shown in the cast sheets too).
Feature 34 (§10.23): `bibC` (the `bib` text's colour, default #1b3a8a; one texture per text and
colour), `hatBand` (the bucket's band, default its colour × 0.62), `hatSun` (SunTrip's sun on the
bucket's front: a yellow disc on the crown's slope with a red bar for the letters), `noseGuard` (a
white plastic shell over the nose, its own ellipsoid grown 1.25 × 1.15 × 1.3 and 0.08 R forward, and
a tab up to the bridge).
Prints (shirt and dress) are a second mesh without an outline (one extra
draw call on printed models; the cabin and Rio busts keep them merged); under a `suit` or a `vest`
the shirt print is a few dots in the V or the vest's opening only. An outfit clears a base field with
`null` (e.g. the flyg cardigans drop the dress print).
Carmencita's scarf, Städerskan's apron, the Grisfestvärd's sash and a real `hat: 'cap'` replace the
Phase 0 stand-ins. Content may give an outfit a `held` field or use the `giraffe`, `butterKnife`,
`film`, `mirror` or `shoeOff` anim flags, which bring their own props.

Anim flags on `Character.anim` (Phase 0 adds them all with a minimal arm pose where noted; WP-E
polishes): `wings` (arms straight out — Phase 0), `cupUp` (right arm up+forward, empty-handed —
Phase 0; the luggage stowers' arm at the rack and the carried juice, which is its own mesh),
`cupHeld` (Phase 3 r2: the `cup` prop in the right hand, raised like `cupUp` when seated — Stig's
"Ja." in juice, §8.3 — and held out at shoulder height standing — the trolley stewardess serving,
§5.8; feature 47, §10.32: with `cupUp` as well it is raised standing too, the right arm (−2.75, 0,
−0.08), the neck tipped back 0.3 to look up at it — Stig under Viking Bar's lamp),
`push` (both arms forward at waist — Phase 0), `planeSeat` (seated, arms on armrests — Phase 0),
`hold` (arms out to the sides low — Phase 0), `flail` (Phase 0), `oath` (right hand up, left on
chest — Phase 0), `dance` (Phase 0: cheer variant), `laugh`, `slump`, `shoeOff`, `mirror`, `film`,
`giraffe`, `butterKnife`, `carryOver` (WP-E), `glide` (feature 3, §10.7: legs together, the
body tipped 0.28 forward and rocking, leaning by the numeric `anim.bank` (+ = his right); with
`wings` for the arms), `swan` (feature 4, §10.8: a swan dive's arms out and a little back, chin
up, legs together, the body tipped 0.5 forward; a look only, unlike `wings` it leaves the wish
alone). `anim.look` (radians added to the neck's yaw) is the glide's dazed shake. `camShow` (feature 47, §10.32): Ole showing his camera, the `camera`
prop (Herr Storch's) held out at the chest between both hands (right arm (−1.25, 0, 0.5), left
(−1.2, 0, −0.5)), its lens to the one he shows it to, his head bent to it (0.22); `heldPose` counts
it as busy, and a `held: 'camera'` def leaves the prop to it, as to `film`. `anim.card`
(feature 4, not a boolean flag: a string, or null/undefined for none) holds the `scoreCard` prop
(a stick and a 0.6 × 0.42 board, its number a face plane on each side drawn once per string by
`textCanvas`) out in the right hand at shoulder to eye height, off to her right (right arm

`calc` (feature 30, §10.10): Ole's calculator alarm held up high in the **left** hand (the near one
as he stands at the head of Stig's bed facing him; left arm (−0.45 ± a 13/s shake, 0, 2.55)), the

neck tipped back a little; `heldPose` counts it as busy.
`ski` (feature 7, §10.12): the rollerskier's kit and stride. A red rollerski under each shoe
(`skiR`/`skiL` props on the legs: a 0.74 m plank, the binding, a black wheel at each end; the body
rides `SKI_LIFT` 0.11 m up on them and the skis stay level) and a pole in each hand (`poleR`/`poleL`:
the grip at the hand, the shaft to a hard tip `POLE_LEN` 1.32 m below). Moving, he double-poles on
`m.phase` at half the walking rate (no leg swing): the push (42 % of a cycle) from the arms high in
front (−1.25) to back (0.55), bending at the hips up to 0.6 and dipping, then the arms swing forward;
blended in by speed up to 2.5 m/s. Each pole is aimed so its tip reaches the ground (in the
recovery up to 0.35 m over it) from the hand's height over his soles, laid back and a little out;
standing, the poles rest forward and out with the hands on the grips. With `wave` (the base pose's

but while Stig has them, §10.39), so the cast sheets show the base look; `game.skis` sets it on

`glide` rolls with the hips leaned 0.34, the arms back (0.45) and the tips trailing 0.3 m off the
ground, `wobble` flails both arms up and out (z ±2.45, swinging) with the poles along them, rocking;
none (the skier) is the stride above. A body without a `bib` of its own wears `skiBib` (a prop-like
mesh in `m.props`, hidden with them): a white ESLÖV race number with a red edge on a 1.5 rad strip of
the torso's elliptic cylinder at 0.58 of its height (`m.T` keeps the torso's size from
`buildCharacter`). Flung or down (`skiFallen`) the skis stay on his feet, level in the hips' frame
(lying on his back: straight up in the air) and the poles point on along his arms; before feature 71
a fall hid the skier's kit.

asleep, lolling, the mouth open), `lift` (0..1) raising the head 0.55 off the backrest and stopping
the loll. `slump`'s own poses skip a lying body. Feature 57 (§10.33): flat on the sand `lean` is −π/2;
`arms` may be [[R], [L]], the two arms' rotations as given; `roll` turns the whole body about its own
long axis (`body.rotation.y`, + its front to its left) and `turn` the head (+ to its left).
`STEKT_SKIN` 0xf0705a is the `stekt` outfits' skin (Berra's and Robban's island looks, lobster red).

**character.js**: `ch.setDef(def)` (rebuild model under the same parent; keep x/y/z/yaw/state;
`height` updated); state `'hidden'` (step no-op, `root.visible = false`, skipped by
`carsVsPeople`); `ch.seatAt({ x, y, z, yaw })` (state `seated`, `anim.planeSeat`, root placed by
hand at hip height, `x/y/z` set for bubbles); `ch.standAt(x, z, yaw)` (state `normal`, teleport).
`ch.tumble(secs, roll)` (feature 3, §10.7; only from `normal`): state `down` for `secs`, the first
`roll` s a forward roll about his own right axis (root rotation order `YXZ`, turning about his
middle, lifted so nothing goes under the floor) onto his back, then lying on his back along his
own heading; his vx/vz carry the roll on (decaying at 6/s, walls collide, never onto a floor more
than 0.3 m off); at the end order `XYZ`, `onGetUp`. `fling` cancels it. `GRAV` (24) is exported.
`ch.flop(secs)` (feature 4, §10.8; only from `normal`): state `down` for `secs`, face down along his
own heading, head first (root order `YXZ`, x = π/2, lifted 0.25 as any `down`), then order `XYZ`,
`onGetUp`; `fling` cancels it. The `down` pose spreads his arms and legs: the belly flop.
The nap (feature 30, §10.10) lays him on his bed with `tumble(1e9, 1e-3)` and `tumbleT = 1` (past
the roll: on his back, head along −his heading, so heading the bed's yaw puts it on the pillow) and
ends it by hand (`state 'normal'`, `tumbleT` null, order `XYZ`, a teleport to the bed's foot).
`ch.lieAt({ x, y, z, yaw, lean, arms, tilt, lift })` (feature 32, §10.22): state `lying` (step a
no-op, no physics; `carsVsPeople` and every `state === 'normal'` rule pass it by): `sync` puts the
hips at (x, y, z) (`x/y/z` are the hips: bubbles anchor at the head top as ever), the root `legLen`
below them along his up axis leaned back `lean` (order `YXZ`), heading `yaw`; `liePose` is the pose,
read by `anim.lie`. `fling(vx, vy, vz, flip)` (feature 32): `flip` (rad/s, negative backwards) makes
the flight a somersault about his own right axis (order `YXZ`) from the lean he had, instead of the
tumble about the world's X; landing (`down`) sets order `XYZ` again. Any state but `seated`/`hidden`
may be flung, `lying` included (its `liePose` dropped). In any other state `sync` sets order `XYZ`
back unless a tumble, a flop or a flip holds `YXZ`.
`ch.wade` (feature 8, §10.13; metres, default 0): in state `normal` `sync` sets the root that far
below his feet (`y − wade`), so in the pool the water plane hides his legs (waist-deep at 0.5);
physics, bubbles' anchors and `ch.y` are unchanged. Only `game.fest` sets it (easing it, `wadeTo`).

**main.js `carsVsPeople`** (Phase 3 r1 repair): a car knocks a `normal` character over (`fling`,
`onCharHit`) only when its **own** speed into him (`car.v · n`, n from the car to him) is over
4.5 m/s; slower contact only pushes him out. Bigmouth used the relative speed, so anyone who
walked (island 5.4 m/s) or sprinted (8.8) into a parked car, or sprinted (5.2) into the stopped
trolley (a kinematic car with v = 0), was flung as if run over. The trolley's bowling is
cabin.js's own rule (§5.8).

export const CAR_TYPES = {...};                       // §6.6
export function registerCarType(key, spec)            // used by cabin.js for 'trolley'
// buildCarModel: `if (s.build) return s.build(s, color);` first (it may return { geo, glass, extras });
// wheels skipped when s.noWheels; glass null-guarded (existing). spec flags: livery
// ('suntrip'|'guagua'), guardia, taxi, pigs, hatch, wagon, colors (random colour palette).
// car fields: noEnter (never offered to the player), noExplode (damage → dead + fx.steam, no fire,
// no burn), isPursuer, riders[], decals[].
// car.repaint(color, { dala = false }) (feature 1, §7.2): rebuilds the body and its outline in
// `color` (the colour is baked into vertex colours), keeps glass, wheels, liveries and occupants;
// `dala` adds the dalahäst dress once (white flowers with yellow eyes and green leaves on the doors
// and bonnet, the white-green-blue harness and a saddle; vans: two flowers and the harness) as an
// unoutlined decal mesh `car.dala` in decals[] (a burn hides it). car.painted: set by the paint shop.
// Occupants (Phase 2, §6.6): car.seatY() (bust base / hips − 0.12, car-local), car.roofY() (roof
// underside − 0.08; buses too), car.fitScale(h, base = seatY()) = clamp((roofY − base) / h,
// 0.72, 1). main.addBust / addRider (not 'bed') / seat use them, so no head pokes through a roof.
// Feature 121 (§6.6, §10.54): spec `seat` sets seatY and the seats' spots (car.seatAt(side): main.seat,
// addBust, seatWorld), `open` makes roofY seatY + 2.5, `height` overrides car.height, `wb` the steering's
// wheelbase, `wheels` the axles (each wheel { piv, mesh, front, k }: it turns at k = wheelR / r).
// The grisbil's pigs (feature 15, §10.15): export PIG_SLOTS ([x, z / len, yaw, scale] on the bed
// floor) and pigMesh(scale) (an outlined pig, feet at 0, snout +z; built once per scale and
// cloned); a `pigs` car gets car.pigs[i] = { mesh, in } in its tilt group (empty otherwise);
// car.setPig(i, on) (hidden while off, or on a burnt wreck); car.pigWorld(i, out?) -> { x, y, z }
// its spot in world space; damage's burn hides them, repair shows the ones `in`.
// car.lift (feature 20, §10.17; default 0): the nose raised that many rad about the rear wheels
// (sync adds it to the pitch and lifts the tilt group by sin(lift) × the rear axle's distance), for
// the car on the GRÚA truck's hook. car.lappSlip: the parking slip's mesh in its tilt group, or null.
